contract_revision: 1.3 (2026-07-23 R3: event-type vocabulary is now the SINGLE SOURCE loaded by server machine_store AND client diag_events — the R3-1a never-again gate for cross-contract drift; adds fw_identity (the poison-pill type the daemon emitted but the vocab omitted, reopening R2-6/R2-12), fw_identity_missing, outbox_quarantine, maintenance_overdue; per-record ingest (rejected[] response, batch never all-or-nothing); heartbeat_post lease endpoint (R3-2); record_kinds for the durable JSONL outbox (events + cycles single write path, R3-3))

delivery_identity.semantics: R2-12 (2026-07-21): the Pi stamps every event + cycle record with a delivery identity — source_id (stable device id, default hostname; env WSL_DIAG_SOURCE_ID), boot_id (fresh uuid per daemon process start) and seq (process-wide monotonic counter). The daily diag JSONL file is the outbox: lane_node/diag_events.OutboxReplayer tails it with a persisted cursor advanced ONLY on a 2xx (cursor-ack). The server dedupes on UNIQUE(source_id, boot_id, seq) via INSERT OR IGNORE, so replay overlap after a drop or lost ack is idempotent. Identity is all-or-nothing WITHIN one record: a record carrying only part of the identity triple is rejected (per-record, into the R3-1b 'rejected' list — NOT a whole-batch 400); a record with none inserts as before (legacy live-sink era).

description: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the machine-diagnostics HTTP contract between the Pi lane-node daemon (client: lane_node/diag_events.py HttpSink), the :8766 lane-node server (server/lane_node_server.py + server/machine_store.py), and the WSL Systems bridge (wsl_phase8_bridge.py). Established closing Codex NO-GO audit finding H4 (2026-07-21): the cycle POST wrapper mismatch survived because each side's tests validated against their own fake. BOTH repos' test suites load this file and verify their side against it; change it only with a matching change on every consumer plus the recorded sha256 (server/machine_contract.sha256).

auth.posture: required on every POST when LANE_NODE_TOKEN is set; GETs stay open (LAN-internal)

events_post.ingest_semantics: R3-1b (2026-07-23): PER-RECORD, never all-or-nothing. Every valid record in the batch inserts; every invalid record is returned in 'rejected' as {index, error} and does NOT block the rest. The response is always 2xx for a well-formed JSON array body (the cursor-ack), so a poison-pill record can never stall the outbox cursor — the client (lane_node/diag_events.OutboxReplayer) quarantines rejected records (quarantine file + counter + 'outbox_quarantine' event) and advances past them. A malformed BODY (not a JSON array/object) is still a 400.

event_ack_post.body_value: wsl.db staff id — integer or null, OPAQUE across the domain boundary

machine_health_get.lane_entry_bridge_keys_note: the keys wsl_phase8_bridge._parse_machine_health whitelists and wsl_machine_alerts.observe_health consumes; fault-latch fields come from the NEWEST OPEN fault event, never last_event_*
machine_health_get.lane_entry_state_note: R2-10 (2026-07-21): every configured machine lane (env WSL_MACHINE_LANES, default 21,22) ALWAYS appears with an explicit state from vocab.states — a board the store never heard from is UNKNOWN, never omitted. Lease: last_seen is the newest daemon-heard-from timestamp (WS HELLO/HEARTBEAT + machine ingest, EXCLUDING code deploy_marker:*); age_s = seconds since last_seen (null when never seen). Derivation precedence: MAINTENANCE > (no lease -> UNKNOWN) > (age_s > WSL_MACHINE_LEASE_S, default 90 -> OFFLINE) > (open fault -> FAULT) > HEALTHY. The WSL bridge degrades any snapshot it cannot refresh past its stale bound to UNKNOWN with the snapshot age.

maintenance_post.note: mechanic flag; while on, the lane's health state is MAINTENANCE and WSL-side SMS alerting is suppressed. R3-10 (2026-07-23): maintenance is no longer indefinite — once it has been on longer than WSL_MACHINE_MAINTENANCE_MAX_S (default 43200s / 12h) the server emits ONE 'maintenance_overdue' warn event so a machine left flagged does not silently suppress alerts forever; the state stays MAINTENANCE (the mechanic must clear it), but the overdue event routes to the desk.

health_get_identity.note: R2-8 (2026-07-21): /api/health carries the deployed lane-node short git hash (null when unresolvable). deploy.ps1 on WSL-SRV records + compares it across deploys; only the identity fields are contract-pinned, the rest of /api/health is server-internal.

heartbeat_post.note: R3-2 (2026-07-23): the controller_daemon posts this on a fixed cadence WELL UNDER the lease window (WSL_MACHINE_HEARTBEAT_S default 20s vs WSL_MACHINE_LEASE_S 90s) so a healthy-but-quiet Track-B controller — which sends NO scoring-WS heartbeat (that path is Track-A only, the R3-2/R2-10 wrong-topology bug) — keeps its lease fresh and reads HEALTHY, while a killed controller expires OFFLINE. The server touches machine_leases.last_seen identically to the WS HELLO/HEARTBEAT and ingest paths, and records the carried board/firmware/contract identity. 'outbox' is the R3-3 health block {oldest_unsent_age_s, backlog, cursor_ok, quarantined}. Behind the same X-Lane-Token gate; NOT gated by WSL_MACHINE_DIAG (liveness must survive a diagnostics-ingest kill-switch, same rule as touch_lanes).

vocab.record_kinds_note: R3-3 (2026-07-23): the daily JSONL file is the SINGLE durable write path for BOTH events and cycles. Each outbox line carries an optional '_kind' discriminator ('event' default when absent — the legacy shape; 'cycle' routes the line to /api/machine/cycles wrapped as {cycle: row}). This retires the lossy in-memory-only CycleShipper-without-replay: a cycle written to the outbox survives a crash/outage and replays with the same delivery-identity idempotency as events. The OutboxReplayer cursor recovery scans from the OLDEST file carrying unshipped records, never the newest (the R3-3 stranding bug).
